osteo.name: Osteopathy
osteo.lead: Professional, hands-on osteopathy to help reduce pain, improve movement and support long term musculoskeletal health.
osteo.introTitle: Osteopathic treatment at Lichfield Osteopathic Practice
intro: Whether you're dealing with back pain, neck stiffness, headaches, joint problems, or ongoing aches and strains, osteopathy offers a hands-on, whole body approach tailored to you.
We welcome patients of all ages from Lichfield and the surrounding areas, offering calm, thorough care in a supportive clinical setting.
ticks: Patients of all ages, from babies to later life
Caring for patients in Lichfield since 1983
osteo.introAlt: An osteopath treating a patient's arm and shoulder

sections.title: What is osteopathy?
paras: Osteopathy is a form of manual therapy that focuses on how the body's muscles, joints, ligaments and nervous system work together. Osteopaths use skilled hands-on techniques to assess and treat restrictions that may be contributing to pain or reduced movement.
Rather than only treating symptoms, osteopathy looks at the wider picture to understand why pain has developed and how best to support recovery.

sections.title: Who is osteopathy for?
paras: Osteopaths' patients include the young, the more mature person, manual workers, office professionals, pregnant women, children and sports people.
Our team covers a broad spectrum of osteopathic skills, including classical, cranial and paediatric osteopathy, sports injuries and functional medicine.

techniques.d: Gentle movement of stiff or restricted joints.
Muscle and soft tissue techniques to ease tension.
Stretching and movement work as part of your treatment.
Advice on posture, activity and recovery.

osteo.condsLead: Patients see us for a wide variety of problems. Not sure if we can help? Call us for a quick chat before you book.
conds: Posture problems from driving or work

steps.d: Your first appointment starts with a detailed case history.
Careful observation and examination, using palpation (feel through touch) to find areas of restriction, strain and weakness.
We explain the diagnosis. By the second treatment your osteopath can usually tell you how many treatments are likely to be needed.
You may feel a little sore or achy for up to 48 hours. Most people usually start feeling better after this.

faqs.q: What is osteopathy recommended for?
faqs.a: Patients seek treatment for a wide variety of conditions, including back pain, shoulder and neck pain, knee and ankle pain, repetitive strain injuries, changes to posture in pregnancy, postural problems caused by driving or work strain, the pain of arthritis and most sports injuries.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: The number of sessions you need depends on the condition and the person we are treating. The aim is to keep your appointments to a minimum. Your osteopath will usually be able to tell you by the second treatment how many treatments are likely to be required, and this will be discussed with you after the diagnosis has been explained at your initial assessment.

faqs.q: What can I expect at my first session?
faqs.a: Your initial consultation will include a detailed case history, as well as careful observation and examination using highly developed skills of palpation (feel through touch) to find areas of restriction, strain and weakness in the body.

faqs.q: How will I feel after a treatment?
faqs.a: There is the possibility of feeling a little sore or achy for up to 48 hours after a treatment. Most people will usually start feeling better after this.

paediatric.name: Baby & Paediatric Osteopathy
paediatric.lead: Gentle, specialist osteopathy for babies and infants to help support comfort, movement and healthy development during the early months of life.
paediatric.introTitle: Baby osteopathy at Lichfield Osteopathic Practice
intro: Babies can experience strain from pregnancy and birth, even when delivery has gone smoothly. Gentle osteopathic treatment aims to reduce tension, support normal movement patterns and help babies feel more settled.
We regularly see families from Lichfield and the surrounding areas looking for a safe, natural approach to support their baby's wellbeing.
ticks: Soft, hands-on treatment using light pressure
We work at your baby's pace
Parents are encouraged to ask questions

sections.title: Why parents bring their baby
paras: Parents often seek baby osteopathy for concerns such as colic, feeding difficulties, unsettled sleep or a preference to turn the head one way.
These issues can be associated with birth factors such as prolonged labour, assisted delivery, caesarean section or breech positioning, but they can also occur without an obvious cause.

sections.title: Cranial osteopathy
paras: Cranial osteopathy is part of the broad spectrum of osteopathic skills our team covers. It is a very gentle approach, which is why it is often used with babies and young children.
Osteopathy is suitable for all ages, from birth to seniority.

paediatric.condsTitle: Common reasons parents bring their baby
paediatric.condsLead: Every baby is different. If you're unsure whether osteopathy is right for your baby, call us for a quick chat.
conds: Flat head or head shape concerns

steps.d: A detailed discussion about pregnancy, birth, feeding and sleep.
Gentle observation of your baby's posture and movement.
Soft, hands-on treatment using light pressure and subtle techniques. We'll always explain what we are doing.
You're welcome to hold or feed your baby during the session if needed.

faqs.q: Can I hold or feed my baby during the appointment?
faqs.a: Yes. We work at your baby's pace, and you are welcome to hold or feed your baby during the session if needed.

faqs.q: What causes these problems?
faqs.a: Babies can experience strain from pregnancy and birth, even when delivery has gone smoothly. Problems can be associated with birth factors such as prolonged labour, assisted delivery, caesarean section or breech positioning, but they can also occur without an obvious cause.

faqs.q: Will my baby improve?
faqs.a: Many parents notice improvements in comfort, feeding or sleep following treatment, although every baby responds differently.

massage.name: Sports & Deep Tissue Massage
massage.h1: Deep Tissue & Sports Massage in Lichfield
massage.lead: Expert deep tissue and sports massage to help relieve muscle tension, improve mobility and support recovery from physical strain or injury.
massage.introTitle: Deep tissue & sports massage in Lichfield
intro: This style of massage uses firmer pressure and targeted techniques to work into deeper layers of muscle and connective tissue.
It's ideal for active individuals, those with physically demanding jobs, or anyone experiencing persistent tightness or muscle discomfort.
ticks: Treatments are always tailored to you
Pressure adjusted so the work is effective but controlled
Sports, deep tissue or pregnancy massage
massage.introAlt: A deep tissue massage of the upper back

sections.title: Tailored to you
paras: Treatments are always tailored to you, with pressure adjusted to ensure the work is effective but controlled.
Choose sports, deep tissue or pregnancy massage, in a 60 or 90 minute session.

sections.title: Massage alongside osteopathy
paras: Massage may be used on its own or alongside osteopathic treatment, depending on your symptoms and goals. We'll always discuss the most appropriate approach and what to expect following treatment.

massage.condsTitle: Who deep tissue & sports massage is for
massage.condsLead: Deep tissue and sports massage can be particularly helpful if you're experiencing any of these.
conds: Neck, shoulder or lower back pain
Muscle fatigue from training or manual work
Recovery issues after activity or competition

steps.d: We discuss your symptoms and goals, and the most appropriate approach.
Firmer pressure and targeted techniques, adjusted so the work is effective but controlled.
We'll explain what to expect following treatment.

faqs.q: How firm is the pressure?
faqs.a: Deep tissue and sports massage uses firmer pressure, but treatments are always tailored to you, with pressure adjusted to ensure the work is effective but controlled.

faqs.q: Can massage be combined with osteopathy?
faqs.a: Yes. Massage may be used on its own or alongside osteopathic treatment, depending on your symptoms and goals.

faqs.q: Do you offer pregnancy massage?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose sports, deep tissue or pregnancy massage, in a 60 minute (£60) or 90 minute (£80) session.

physio.name: Physiotherapy
physio.lead: Thorough assessment and structured rehab to rebuild strength, restore function and get you back to what you love.
intro: Recovering from a sports injury, living with a persistent joint problem or struggling to get back to full strength after an operation? Physiotherapy gives you a clear, step-by-step route back.
We combine hands-on treatment with a progressive exercise programme built around your goals, whether that's running a 10k, lifting your grandchildren or getting through the working day without pain.
ticks: Registered physiotherapist with a sports science background
Rehab programmes you can follow at home
Works hand-in-hand with osteopathy and massage

sections.title: What is physiotherapy?
paras: Physiotherapy helps restore movement and function when you're affected by injury, illness or disability. It uses movement, exercise, manual therapy and education to get to the root of the problem.
The focus is on you playing an active part in your recovery, so the results last beyond the treatment room.

sections.title: How we approach rehabilitation
paras: Your first session is a detailed assessment of how you move, where you're weak or restricted and what's driving your symptoms. From there we build a plan with clear milestones.
Exercises are introduced at the right time and progressed as you improve, so you're always working at the right level.

sections.title: When should I start?
paras: The sooner the better. Early, guided rehab often shortens recovery and reduces the chance of a problem becoming long-term. If you're recovering from surgery, we'll follow your consultant's guidance.

techniques.d: Personalised, progressive programmes you can do at home or in the gym.
Hands-on joint and soft tissue techniques to ease pain and stiffness.
Looking at how you squat, lunge, run or lift to find the weak link.
Building capacity so you're stronger than before the injury.
Structured recovery after joint replacements and other surgery.
Clear criteria for getting back to training safely.

physio.condsLead: Not sure if your problem is on the list? Call us for a quick chat before you book.

steps.d: We take a full history, covering your symptoms, health, work, activity and what you want to get back to.
We look at how you move and test the structures involved to find what's driving the problem.
We explain what we've found in plain language and agree a plan with clear goals.
Where it's appropriate we start treatment the same day, and send you home with simple things to do.

faqs.q: Do I need a GP referral?
faqs.a: No. You can book directly with us. Some insurers ask for a referral before they'll cover treatment, so it's worth checking.

faqs.q: What's the difference between osteopathy and physiotherapy?
faqs.a: There's a lot of overlap. Osteopathy tends to lead with hands-on treatment, while physiotherapy often leads with exercise-based rehab. We'll guide you to whichever suits your problem best, or combine the two.

faqs.q: Will I get exercises to do at home?
faqs.a: Yes. You'll leave with a clear, simple programme, and we'll progress it at each visit.

faqs.q: Can you help after surgery?
faqs.a: Yes. We help people recover after joint replacements, ligament repairs and other operations, following your surgeon's protocol.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: We'll give you an honest estimate at your first appointment and review it as you progress.

laser.name: Laser Therapy
laser.lead: Non-invasive, high-power laser treatment to help ease pain and support healing in stubborn tendon, joint and muscle problems.
laser.introTitle: A modern option for stubborn pain
intro: Some problems, like long-standing tendon pain or a joint that just won't settle, don't respond as well as we'd like to hands-on treatment and exercise alone. Laser therapy can be a useful addition to your plan.
It's quick, painless for most people and needs no downtime, so you can carry on with your day straight afterwards.
ticks: Usually combined with hands-on treatment and rehab
Assessed by a clinician before every course
laser.introAlt: Laser therapy being given to a patient's knee

sections.title: What is laser therapy?
paras: High-power laser therapy uses focused light energy that's absorbed by the tissues. It's used to help reduce pain and inflammation and to support the body's natural healing processes.

sections.title: How treatment works
paras: After an assessment, your clinician moves the laser handpiece over the area for a few minutes. Most people feel a gentle warmth. You'll wear protective glasses during treatment.
A course is usually a series of short sessions alongside your other treatment, and we'll review progress as we go.

sections.title: Is it right for me?
paras: Laser therapy isn't suitable for everyone. For example, it isn't used over a pregnancy, certain cancers or some skin conditions. We'll check your medical history carefully and only recommend it if we think it's a good fit.

techniques.d: We confirm the diagnosis and check suitability first.
Short, targeted sessions over the affected area.
Paired with osteopathy, physio or massage for best results.
Guidance on activity while tissues settle.
Strengthening to help stop the problem returning.
Regular check-ins so you know it's working.

laser.condsTitle: What laser therapy can help with
laser.condsLead: Not sure if your problem is on the list? Call us for a quick chat before you book.

steps.d: We take a full history, covering your symptoms, health, work, activity and what you want to get back to.
We look at how you move and test the structures involved to find what's driving the problem.
We explain what we've found in plain language and agree a plan with clear goals.
Where it's appropriate we start treatment the same day, and send you home with simple things to do.

faqs.q: Does laser therapy hurt?
faqs.a: Most people feel only a gentle, soothing warmth. Tell your clinician if it feels too warm and they'll adjust it.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: It varies by condition. We'll suggest a course after your assessment and review how you're responding.

faqs.q: Is it safe?
faqs.a: When delivered by a trained clinician with eye protection and proper screening, it's a low-risk treatment. We'll go through any reasons it might not be suitable for you.

faqs.q: Can I have it with other treatment?
faqs.a: Yes. It usually works best as part of a wider plan including hands-on treatment and exercise.

faqs.q: Is there any downtime?
faqs.a: No. You can return to normal activities straight away.

acupuncture.name: Acupuncture
acupuncture.lead: Western medical acupuncture and dry needling to help ease persistent muscle and joint pain, as part of your treatment plan.
intro: Western medical acupuncture uses very fine, single-use needles placed into specific points and tight muscles to help reduce pain and ease tension. It's based on modern understanding of anatomy and the nervous system.
We usually use acupuncture alongside hands-on treatment and exercise, rather than on its own, to help calm pain so you can move and recover more comfortably.
ticks: Combined with hands-on treatment and rehab
acupuncture.introAlt: Acupuncture needles being placed in a patient's upper back

sections.title: What is acupuncture?
paras: Acupuncture involves inserting very fine needles into the skin and muscle. In Western medical acupuncture and dry needling, needles are placed into tight muscles and specific points to help reduce pain.
NICE recommends acupuncture as an option for some people with chronic primary pain, and to help prevent tension-type headaches and migraines.

sections.title: What a session involves
paras: After an assessment, needles are placed and usually left in for a short time while you relax. Most people feel only a small pinprick, followed by a dull ache or heaviness that soon settles.

sections.title: Is it right for me?
paras: Acupuncture isn't suitable for everyone, for example if you have a bleeding disorder, take blood thinners or have a fear of needles. We'll check your medical history and talk through the options.

techniques.d: Fine needles at specific points to ease pain.
Targeted needling of tight muscle knots.
Paired with osteopathy or physio.
Sterile and disposed of after each use.
Checking suitability before every course.
We track how you're responding.

acupuncture.condsLead: Not sure if your problem is on the list? Call us for a quick chat before you book.

steps.d: We take a full history, covering your symptoms, health, work, activity and what you want to get back to.
We look at how you move and test the structures involved to find what's driving the problem.
We explain what we've found in plain language and agree a plan with clear goals.
Where it's appropriate we start treatment the same day, and send you home with simple things to do.

faqs.q: Does acupuncture hurt?
faqs.a: Most people feel a small pinprick and then a dull ache or heaviness. It's usually far less uncomfortable than people expect.

faqs.q: Is it the same as Chinese acupuncture?
faqs.a: Western medical acupuncture uses similar needles but is based on modern anatomy and physiology rather than traditional Chinese medicine.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: Often a course of several sessions. We'll review how you respond and only continue if it's helping.

faqs.q: Can it be added to my osteopathy appointment?
faqs.a: Yes. Acupuncture is often used as part of an osteopathy session.
